# rawsock — spec

## Maturity

**Grade:** 3 · S3 E1 A2 H1 P3 · limited by scope (core), performance (over 1.1× the reference) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** parity — libpcap 1.10.6 on Linux (live capture incl. an opt-in `TPACKET_V3` ring; the `pcap_compile` filter language incl. `vlan`, offline and in the live ancillary form alone and combined, over Ethernet, Linux cooked v1 and v2, raw IP, DLT_NULL and DLT_LOOP; classic pcap + pcapng savefiles). Also `inbound`, `outbound`, `ifindex`, `pppoed`, and `mpls` / `pppoes` ALONE; NOT built: `mpls` / `pppoes` combined with other primitives and `geneve` (not built: budget, Backlog); every other libpcap feature a Linux user would notice is rejected with a reason or deferred (see "What is deliberately not done" and Backlog) (surveyed 2026-11-04)

**Audit:** review 2026-10-04 · mutation 2026-10-04 (39/41, 2 eq) · src ?

The audit above predates the 2026-11-03 code. That code has only mutant schemata: 2026-11-03 `run`, `validate`, long jumps, a grammar subset, pcapng, ring (32 mutants, 31 killed, 1 equivalent) and 2026-11-04 names/shorthand grammar, `Ring.init` limits, the new links, live vlan and release ticket (27 mutants, all killed after two new tests). The live socket paths were not mutated.

**Hardening:** fuzz 2026-11-04 (200,000 runs per harness, ReleaseSafe test binary run directly in `unshare -rn`, `runs=200000` lines seen on all 10 harnesses, 139 tests; the filter harness drives every link and both vlan forms and reaches the run-time vlan form and the new links, asserted) · ct n/a — raw sockets (keyword review, 2026-10-07) · panic 2026-10-30 (sweep + blind review: filter compile stack overflow on long and/or chains (leaf cap; a loop for left-deep chains and parser nesting 16 since 2026-11-04, the deepest accepted inputs compile in a 64 KiB stack, tested), run jump saturation, cmsg/pcap totality, ifname NUL; delta audit 32/36 + 4 eq); 2026-11-04 sweep entries for every link, both vlan forms, `runLive` and `Link.fromDlt`

**Performance:** ref 0.98× libpcap 1.10.6 source build (worst row `compile`; `filter_run` 0.93×, `filter_run_lp` 0.87×) · fastest ? (on the filter and compile rows no other implementation has the language, so there is nothing to be fastest against; the savefile rows have gopacket pcapgo, slower than ours, and the Rust `pcap-file` crate, info rows that do not feed this field) (measured 2026-11-04, `bench-rawsock`, ReleaseFast, 21 rounds, best of each side, wall time, WITHOUT `-Djcc-safe`, shared noisy host, spreads 8–45 %). **P2 rests on the SOURCE build** (libpcap from the pinned tag, CMake `Release` `-O3`, static, built by the coordinator, `LIBPCAP=…/libpcap.a`). The distro build of the same source (libpcap.so.0.8) is not another implementation and is not the `fastest` field; against it only two rows were measured: `filter_run` 1.14× (spread 8.8 %) and `filter_run_lp` 1.03× (7.7 %), 21 rounds, no `-Djcc-safe`; ours executes fewer instructions (0.93×) at a lower IPC (1.61 against 2.04), i.e. 1.18× the cycles; unprofiled (Backlog has the `perf` commands). Its `compile` and savefile rows and a `-Djcc-safe` run against it were NOT measured: all four attempts were OOM-killed at the bench's Go step (see the report). Ours/libpcap (source build) per row: `compile` 0.98, `filter_run` 0.93 (both sides run the SAME 8 programs ours compiled: interpreter against interpreter), `filter_run_lp` 0.87 (libpcap's own optimised programs), `pcap_read` 0.15, `pcap_write` 0.55, `pcapng_read` 0.21 — these three time libpcap's `fmemopen`/stdio read or write with a per-packet copy, different work from our slice parser, so they are not a speed claim; info `compile_opt` 0.13. `perf stat -e instructions:u,cycles:u` for `filter_run` per operation (N=3000 minus N=500): ours 3.23 M instructions and 2.01 M cycles, libpcap source build 3.43 M and 2.21 M (0.94 and 0.91). `-Djcc-safe`, source build, filter rows only: 0.875 / 0.833. An earlier run of the two filter rows: 0.985 / 0.922. Ours/Go (gopacket v1.7.5 pcapgo, x/net v0.55.0 bpf): `pcap_read` 0.12, `pcap_write` 0.56, `pcapng_read` 0.13; the Go VM runs `filter_run` at 2.0× libpcap. Ours/Rust (`pcap-file` 2.0.0 slice parsers, info rows, spread ours/Rust): `pcap_read` 1.135 (5.6 / 6.0 %), `pcap_write` 1.116 (13.5 / 21.0 %), `pcapng_read` 0.875 (16.3 / 13.0 %): equal speed within the noise, no claim either way. Stack: the compile recursion is bounded (parser nesting 16, left-deep chains are a loop) and the deepest accepted inputs compile in a 64 KiB stack (test: LLVM Debug and ReleaseSafe x86_64, self-hosted Debug x86_64 and ReleaseSmall; mips32 Debug, ReleaseSafe and ReleaseSmall under qemu; the same test at 32 KiB passes everywhere except the self-hosted Debug backend, which needs between 32 and 64 KiB, so the margin there is under 2×). Live capture is not a row (the kernel's cost is the same on both sides); `bench-rawsock -- ring` (2026-11-03: `recv` 502 kframes/s with 0.25 % lost, ring 555 with none lost, libpcap 462 with none lost; sender-limited, not a throughput ceiling; not re-run after the release ticket)

**Known defects:** (1) in the live ancillary `vlan` form a failed `vlan` test leaves the run-time shift at 4, so `vlan or ip` and `not vlan and ip` miss a plain untagged IPv4 frame on a live socket (`ip or vlan` does not): libpcap's own live programs do the same (the 42 `tcpdump -i lo -dd` rows agree); (2) `mpls` and `pppoes` work alone only, anything written after them is `UnsupportedExpression` (libpcap shifts the later offsets); (3) offline `ip and vlan` compiles here where libpcap refuses it; (4) `filter_run` is 1.14× the distro libpcap.so in wall time (IPC gap, unprofiled, see Performance); (5) a NULL savefile needs `Options.null_byte_order` when the file may come from the other kind of host.

**Downstream consumer:** yes

Design + threat notes for auditors. Usage: see ./README.md. Attribution/provenance: original work of
the zig-libs authors (MIT).

**Where we are ahead:** the only pure-Zig, libc-free AF_PACKET capture **and** inject path we found: in-kernel classic-BPF attach, promiscuous mode, kernel drop counters (`Socket.stats`), the 802.1Q tag recovered through `PACKET_AUXDATA` (`Frame.vlan_tci` — the kernel strips it before a tap sees the frame, so a naive capture loses it), a `sockaddr_ll` decoder, an ARP codec, and real-segment ARP/IPv4 goldens from a veth pair. **Where we are behind** (re-checked 2026-11-04): no `recvmmsg` batching; no 802.11 / PPP-savefile link layers (Backlog); the generated filter code is unoptimised (longer than libpcap's; the same verdicts except the known `ip and vlan` deviation); no host-name/service-name resolution; Linux only by design (→ "What is deliberately not done"). Built since the survey: `filter.compile`/`run` (2026-10-04; on 2026-11-03 IPv6 `host`/`net`, bare `host`/`net`, `portrange`, `less`/`greater`/`len`, `broadcast`/`multicast`, `proto[off:size] & mask RELOP n` offset expressions, `arp`/`rarp host`), `pcap` savefiles, `pcapng` reader and writer (2026-11-03), `Frame.timestamp_ns`, `Socket.joinFanout`.

## Design & invariants

- **Linux AF_PACKET capture + inject, no libpcap, no libc.** Open a `SOCK_RAW` capture socket for
  one EtherType (or every frame, `eth_p.all`), decode the kernel's `sockaddr_ll` into a typed
  `Frame`, attach an in-kernel classic-BPF filter, toggle promiscuous mode, and cook-inject frames
  on a named interface (a `SOCK_DGRAM` socket where the kernel builds the Ethernet header) or
  transmit a complete frame on the raw socket (`sendRaw`). Original work of the zig-libs authors
  (MIT), starting from a minimal receive-only ~25-LOC core (`openPacketCapture`/`ifNameOf`); the
  send path, `SO_ATTACH_FILTER` filtering, `PACKET_ADD_MEMBERSHIP` promiscuous mode, interface
  lookup by name/index (there is no listing), and the typed `Frame`/`LinkAddr`/`EthHeader` decode are new construction. Wire layout
  clean-room from `packet(7)`, Linux UAPI headers (`<linux/if_packet.h>`, `<linux/if_ether.h>`,
  `<linux/filter.h>`), IEEE 802.3/802.1AB, and ARP, with EtherStruct (BSD-2-Clause) consulted
  only as a header-field-order cross-check (no source copied). libpcap's
  source was read only on 2026-11-04 for the questions in "Compared with"; nothing was ported.
- **Pure helpers need no socket/privilege:** `EthHeader.parse`/`.write`, `parseHwaddr`/
  `formatHwaddr` (MAC ⇄ `"aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff"`), `LinkAddr.fromSockaddr` (the `sockaddr_ll` decode
  `recv` uses), `bpf`/`etherTypeFilter` (classic-BPF program builder; wire-format `BpfInsn` is 8
  bytes, asserted), `arp.buildRequest`/`arp.parseReply` (addresses surface as `netaddr.Ip`).
- **Raw errno syscalls, no libc:** all socket/ioctl calls go through `std.os.linux` directly, a
  conscious ceiling shared with `icmp`/`netlink`. Kernel struct sizes (`sockaddr_ll`, `BpfInsn`) are
  asserted in tests against the documented ABI.
- **Concurrency:** reentrant — no shared state; one `Socket` per thread/loop.

## Filter compiler, savefiles, timestamps, fanout (2026-10-04)

**`filter.compile`.** Recursive descent over the language in `src/filter.zig`'s header (nesting
bounded at 64), an AST of single comparisons (`load [x+]off | #pktlen; [and #mask;] jeq|jset|jge|jgt #k`), and code
generation by true/false labels: `a and b` sends `a`'s false edge to the failure label and its true
edge to `b`; `or` mirrors it; `not` swaps the labels. Every jump is forward, so the program is a
DAG; a jump longer than 255 instructions or a program past `BPF_MAXINSNS` (4096) is
`error.FilterTooComplex`, never a truncated jump. The meaning of each primitive was read off
libpcap's own output (`tcpdump -d`, black box): IPv4 ports require fragment offset 0 and locate
the header with `ldxb 4*([14]&0xf)`; IPv6 transport protocols also match through a fragment
header (44) but IPv6 ports do not walk extension headers; `port` alone is tcp|udp|sctp; `icmp` is
IPv4 only. libpcap's "non-network bits set" refusal for `net` is mirrored.

**`filter.run`.** The kernel's classic-BPF semantics: an out-of-bounds load, a division by zero,
an opcode the kernel would refuse at attach time or running off the end returns 0 (drop); a scratch slot nothing stored to reads 0. One `switch` over the full opcode (2026-11-03; it was a class/size/mode decode plus a zeroed 64-byte scratch array, 2.2× libpcap's interpreter, now 1.05×). It terminates in at most `prog.len`
steps because every instruction advances and no jump goes backwards.

**`pcapng`.** (2026-11-03) Reader: Section Header (either byte order, several sections), Interface Description (`if_tsresol` decimal up to 10^-18 and binary up to 2^-62, `if_tsoffset`, up to `max_interfaces` = 32 per section), Enhanced and Simple Packet blocks; every other block type is skipped by its length. Every block length is checked (multiple of 4, framing, trailer equal, inside the input) before a slice is formed; an instant outside 64-bit nanoseconds is `BadTimestamp`, never wrapped. Writer: host byte order, one interface, `if_tsresol` 6 or 9, EPBs.

**`pcap`.** The writer emits host byte order (as libpcap does); the reader takes either order and
µs or ns magic, and refuses a record longer than `max(snaplen, 262144)` (a corrupt length, not a
frame) or one past the end of the input, before forming any slice. A µs file stores a ns time
truncated, as libpcap does.

**Timestamps.** Best-effort (no new `OpenError`; the module's own example switches on that set
exhaustively, and so may a consumer): `SO_TIMESTAMPNS_NEW` (64-bit `__kernel_timespec` on every arch), falling back to
`SO_TIMESTAMPNS_OLD` on an older 64-bit kernel; the cmsg parser shares the bounded walk of the
`PACKET_AUXDATA` one and rejects a negative time, a nanosecond field ≥ 10⁹ and a u64 overflow.

**Fanout.** One `setsockopt(PACKET_FANOUT, group | (mode | flags) << 16)`; the kernel enforces that
every member agrees on mode and flags, and a test proves the defrag flag reaches it.

## Threat model / out of scope

**Linux-only by design** — no BSD `/dev/bpf` path, no cross-platform abstraction attempted.
**Privilege-gated:** opening a capture/inject socket needs `CAP_NET_RAW`; without it `open` returns
a distinct `error.AccessDenied` rather than a generic failure (interface lookups like `ifaceByName`
are unprivileged and always available). This module is a **capability**, not a policy — it does not
itself restrict which interfaces/EtherTypes a caller may open; that access-control decision belongs
to the deployment (capability grant, network namespace, seccomp). The in-kernel BPF filter
(`setFilter`) reduces what userspace *sees*, it is not a security boundary against a co-resident
process with the same capability. Received frames are attacker-influenced wire data on a shared
L2 segment (spoofable source MAC, malformed lengths); the typed decode (`EthHeader.parse`,
`LinkAddr.fromSockaddr`, `arp.parseReply`) must reject malformed input without panicking — that
tolerant-parsing guarantee is the attack surface to audit, not the socket layer itself. The filter
compiler and the pcap reader take caller-supplied input; both are bounded (nesting depth, program
size, record lengths) and return typed errors. The `TPACKET_V3` ring (`ring.zig`) reads a mapping the kernel writes: every header from it is hostile input (see its header). Out of scope: `recvmmsg`
batching, a TX ring, IPv6 Neighbor Discovery (only ARP is implemented), pcapng blocks other than packets and interface descriptions.

## Verification

Root-free tests (pure helpers, `sockaddr_ll` decode, BPF encoding, struct ABI sizes, fuzz-style
never-panic checks) always run; the socket tests need `CAP_NET_RAW` and `SkipZigTest`
without it. Under an unprivileged network namespace where root has the capability
(`unshare -rn zig build test-rawsock`) all tests pass, including open/filter/promisc and an
inject→capture loopback round-trip on `lo`. **2026-10-04:** the filter compiler is checked frame by frame against libpcap 1.10.6 (`tcpdump
-n -tt -r`) on a 20-frame corpus (ARP; IPv4 TCP/UDP/ICMP/SCTP incl. IP options, both fragment
kinds, a 60-byte IP header; IPv6 TCP/UDP/ICMPv6, a fragment header, next-header 1; a runt; a
frame cut after its IP header; an 802.1Q-tagged frame; an unknown EtherType) for 35 expressions;
`run` is checked on the same corpus with libpcap's own `tcpdump -dd` programs; the pcap codec
reproduces two `tcpdump -w` files byte for byte (µs and ns) and decodes them to the times
`tcpdump -tt -r` printed. Live (netns): `Options.timestamps` lands between send and receive on
CLOCK_REALTIME, a compiled filter attached at open passes only its frame (and the kernel's verdict
equals `run`'s), a fanout group splits round-robin and refuses a member with another mode or
without DEFRAG. Mutation 2026-10-04: 41 mutants, 35 killed, 4 killed by new tests, 2 equivalent
and removed as dead code. Also real-capture goldens: a genuine ARP who-has/
is-at exchange and Ethernet+IPv4 framing captured with `tcpdump` off a real layer-2 segment — a
veth pair with each end in its own throwaway network namespace (`lo` never does ARP, so it can't
anchor this; a real L2 segment is required) — anchoring real Ethernet framing and the ARP wire
layout independently of `buildRequest`/`parseReply` agreeing with themselves. Run:
`zig build test-rawsock` (add `-Doptimize=ReleaseFast` for the release check; `unshare -rn` prefix
for the full socket path).

**2026-11-03 additions.** The new filter primitives are checked on a 30-frame corpus (the 20 above plus ARP who-has, RARP, an IPv6 multicast UDP datagram, a SYN, a SYN-ACK, a 200-byte multicast UDP, an echo request and reply, an IPv6 TCP frame from another prefix, an MF fragment) for 100 expressions: each expression's verdict list is what `tcpdump -n -tt -r` printed (recipe `tools/gen_filter_oracle.py`, which reproduces the corpus and the list byte for byte). pcapng: files converted by Wireshark's `editcap -F pcapng` (black box) decode to the same frames and times as the classic files they came from, and this writer's files are read by `tcpdump -r` and `capinfos` as the same three packets (recipe `tools/gen_pcapng_fixtures.py`). `unshare -rn zig build interop-rawsock` now also asserts `ifaceByName`/`ifaceName`/`hwaddr`/`ipv4Addr`/`ipv4Netmask` against what `ip` configured. Fuzz: `filter.compile` (well-formed program; `E and E` and `E or E` equal `E`; `not (E)` never accepts what `E` accepts), `pcap.Reader` and `pcapng.Reader` (records inside the input, termination, writer round trip), each with a reach assertion. Targets: `-Dtarget=mips-linux-musl -Dcpu=mips32+soft_float -fqemu` (big-endian, ReleaseSafe: 70 pass, 26 skip, only the two BE seed-corpus failures listed in Backlog) and `arm-linux-musleabihf -fqemu` (75 pass, 23 skip, 0 fail).

**2026-11-03 fix round (independent review of the grade-2 pass).** `and`/`or` equal precedence, left to right: `man pcap-filter` (line "Negation has the highest precedence. Alternation and concatenation have equal precedence and associate left to right") and `tcpdump -d 'tcp or udp and port 53'` (compiles to `(tcp or udp) and port 53`); 11 mixed rows are in the oracle. Jump limit: before the fix, 33 `ip host` terms, 14 `tcp port` terms or 5 `port` terms were already `FilterTooComplex` (measured on the pre-fix code); jumps over 255 instructions now go through `ja` stubs, with oracle rows of 40 hosts, 25 `not host`, 30 `portrange` and 25 `ether host` terms and a live attach of a 120-term list (`ja` present, kernel accepts, passes only the last term's frame; netns lane). `run` against the KERNEL (probe `tools/kernel_semantics_probe.py`, Linux 7.0, frames on `lo` through `SO_ATTACH_FILTER`): `ldx #0xffffffff; ld [x+2]` loads offset 1 (the kernel wraps `X + k` in 32 bits); `1 << X` with X = 32 is 1 and with 33 is 2 (the count is masked to five bits); a constant shift of 32 or more, `ld M[k]` before any store, and an offset in `[-0x1000, 0)` that is not an `SKF_AD_*` word are refused at attach (`EINVAL`); `ld [-0x1000]` (`SKF_AD_PROTOCOL`) works; division or modulus by X = 0 drops the frame. `run` now does the same, except negative or ancillary loads, which drop (it has a frame and nothing else; `usesAncillary` says so). Where libpcap's interpreter differs from the kernel (found by the differential below): `X + k` is NOT wrapped there (`X > buflen - k` is a drop, so `ldx #0xffffffff; ld [x+2]` drops in libpcap and loads in the kernel), and `A <<= X` with X >= 32 is undefined behaviour in its C; `run` follows the kernel, the differential avoids both. Differential: 160 seeded random kernel-valid programs (`tools/gen_run_diff.py`, committed table `src/testdata/run_diff.zig`) return the same value in `run` as in libpcap 1.10.6's `pcap_offline_filter` over six frames (169 non-zero cells, 36 distinct values), plus a fuzz harness that runs random valid programs through `validate`, `run` and an independent model (`refRun`) in the same file. One planted mutant (`mul` computed as `add` in `run`) was caught by three tests (the hand-worked ALU table, differential case 54, the fuzz harness). `validate` is the kernel's attach-time check list and every program `compile` emits passes it (asserted on all oracle expressions and inside the compile fuzz harness). pcapng probes against libpcap and Wireshark `capinfos` (files built by hand, see `src/pcapng.zig` tests): a type-2 Packet Block is read by both (now read here); a Simple Packet Block longer than its block is "too short"/"too small" in both (`BadBlock` here, and the old code returned the padding as data when snaplen was 0); `if_tsresol` with length 2 is refused by libpcap and accepted by Wireshark (refused here); decimal resolution above 10^-18 and binary above 2^-62 are accepted by both readers with a meaningless time (`BadTimestamp` here: documented difference); a packet naming an undeclared interface is an error in both; 33 interfaces are fine in both (the reader here caps at `max_interfaces` = 32 because its table has no allocator, 32 x 32 bytes; `TooManyInterfaces`). Differences kept on purpose: none of the above is silently wrong.

**2026-11-04 (grade-2 pass).** Commands, from the repository root: `unshare -rn python3 -I modules/rawsock/tools/gen_link_oracle.py OUT` regenerates `src/testdata/link_oracle.zig` and `vlan_live.zig` from `tcpdump -y DLT -r` and `tcpdump -i lo -dd` (black box; libpcap source was read only to decide `any` = SLL/SLL2 and the savefile AF_INET6 numbers); `unshare -rn sh -c 'ip link set lo up && python3 -I modules/rawsock/tools/protochain_probe.py'`; `unshare -rn zig build interop-rawsock`; the module's test binary (ReleaseSafe) run directly in `unshare -rn`: 129 passed, 0 failed, the 10 fuzz drivers skipped without `RAWSOCK_FUZZ`; with `RAWSOCK_FUZZ=200000` every driver prints `runs=200000` and the run ends `All 139 tests passed`. Targets: mips32 big-endian soft-float under qemu-mips 106 pass 0 fail (33 skipped: no capability), arm32 hard-float under qemu-arm 109 pass 0 fail. A ReleaseSmall program using what axp uses (`Socket.open`, `ifaceByName`, `hwaddr`, `ipv4Addr`, `ipv4Netmask`, `arp.buildRequest`/`parseReply`, `formatHwaddr`, `ifaceName`) is byte-identical before and after this pass: 204160 bytes on mips32 soft-float, 159904 on x86_64 (the new API is not linked into it).

## What is deliberately not done

- **`TPACKET_V3` ring: BUILT 2026-11-03 (`src/ring.zig`).** Opt-in; typed `InitError` (`BadSize`, `AccessDenied`, `RingUnsupported`, `OutOfMemory`); kernel packet/drop/freeze counters; hostile block headers bounded (`Block.init`/`nextPacket`, swept by 8 crafted-header cases, fuzzed); sizes 4 KiB..16 MiB x 2..1024 blocks, 256 MiB total checked in 64 bits; live in the netns (frames delivered, counters, teardown and re-setup, a second ring refused). Not built: `recvmmsg`, TX ring, `PACKET_FANOUT` with the ring, `TPACKET_V2`. Throughput against `recv` and libpcap: see Performance (`bench-rawsock -- ring`; the first harness stalled because libpcap's blocking `pcap_dispatch` never returned under the namespace, fixed with non-blocking reads and a deadline on every wait).
- **Kernel-metadata and MPLS/PPPoE primitives (2026-11-04):** built `inbound`, `outbound` (`ldh [type]`, `SKF_AD_PKTTYPE`, 4 = outgoing) and `ifindex N` (`SKF_AD_IFINDEX`), each checked against `tcpdump -i lo -dd` programs (`vlan_live.zig`: same verdicts under `filter.runLiveMeta` for packet types 0, 3, 4 and two interface indexes) and live on `lo` in a netns (`outbound` passes the frame the socket sent, `inbound` and a foreign `ifindex` drop it, `ifindex <lo>` passes; verdicts equal `runLiveMeta` fed with `Frame.pkttype`/`ifindex`). `mpls [N]` and `pppoes [N]`: built ALONE (EtherType 0x8847 / 0x8864 and the label / session id, rows against the libpcap programs, MPLS and PPPoE frames synthesised in the test); NOT built: the forms combined with other primitives (`mpls and ip` walks the label stack and shifts later offsets, `pppoes and ip` shifts by 8): `UnsupportedExpression`, Backlog "not built: budget". `geneve [N]`: not built, `UnsupportedExpression` (libpcap emits 50 instructions walking the option length through the scratch memory for IPv4 and IPv6 UDP port 6081; no consumer). `ifname`, `rnr`, `ruleset`, `reason`, `action`, `srnr`, `subrulenum`: OpenBSD pflog only (libpcap: "supported only on PF linktype"), refused. `pppoed` built (EtherType 0x8863), `carp` is refused by libpcap itself as an ip proto name. A re-read of `scanner.l` and `man pcap-filter` (2026-11-04) gave every other keyword a verdict: resolver-dependent (`gateway`, names, `ip broadcast`/`multicast`) see the bullet below; 802.11 (`wlan`, `radio`, `type`, `subtype`, `dir`, `ra`, `ta`) Backlog; REJECTED with one reason, no consumer and other link layers (all `UnsupportedExpression`): SS7/MTP (`fisu lssu msu sio opc dpc sls` and the `h*` forms), ATM (`lane oam oamf4 oamf4ec oamf4sc vpi vci connectmsg metaconnect sc ilmic callref bcc`), `decnet lat moprc mopdl sca iso clnp esis isis l1 l2 iih lsp snp csnp psnp stp ipx atalk aarp netbeui llc`, the `fddi`/`tr` qualifiers, and the pflog words `link`/`on`.
- **`vlan` in combination: BUILT** in both forms, with libpcap's shift. Offline (in-packet) form: 18 oracle rows incl. `vlan and vlan 5` (MACs, `multicast`, `ether[..]` unmoved). Live (ancillary, `Options.vlan_ancillary`) form, 2026-11-04: the first `vlan` asks `SKF_AD_VLAN_TAG_PRESENT` / `SKF_AD_VLAN_TAG` and, when the tag is still in the frame, sets the run-time shift in M[0] to 4; later primitives load through `ldx M[0]` (libpcap's `ldx M[1]`, `tcpdump -i lo -d`). 42 programs libpcap compiles for a live Ethernet device (`src/testdata/vlan_live.zig`, recipe `tools/gen_link_oracle.py`) give the same verdicts as ours over thousands of frame/metadata cases (in-frame tags, kernel-stripped tags with priority bits, id 0, QinQ), through `filter.runLive`; one expression differs on purpose: libpcap's own live program for `ip and vlan 5` accepts nothing (it jumps over the `ldh [vlan_tci]`), ours accepts the frame it names. A libpcap quirk ours repeats: a failed `vlan` test leaves the shift at 4, so `vlan or ip` and `not vlan and ip` miss a plain untagged IPv4 frame on a live socket (`ip or vlan` finds it). Live on a kernel: attached on `lo` (tag stays in the frame, PRESENT 0) `vlan 5 and ip` passes only the right frame (root test), and on a veth with a VLAN device (tag stripped, PRESENT 1) `vlan 5 and ether proto 0x88b5` passes and `vlan 5 and ip` does not (`interop-rawsock`). Fixed on the way: the alone form matched a frame whose kernel-stripped tag was not N when a second tag in the frame was N (libpcap decides on the metadata alone); it uses the same code now.
- **Link types:** `Options.link` = `.ethernet`, `.linux_sll`, `.linux_sll2`, `.raw`, `.bsd_null`, `.bsd_loop`, each checked against `tcpdump -y DLT` on savefiles (20 rows for SLL and RAW; 45–55 rows each for NULL, LOOP and cooked v2, `src/testdata/link_oracle.zig`, recipe `tools/gen_link_oracle.py`), refusals included (`ether host`, `multicast`, `vlan`; `arp` on NULL/LOOP). `Link.dlt` / `Link.fromDlt` name the savefile link types (1, 113, 276, 101, 0, 108). DLT_LINUX_SLL2: libpcap's source (`pcap-linux.c`, the `any` device) offers both SLL (the default) and SLL2 in its DLT list, and `tcpdump` 4.99.6 captures `-i any` as SLL2 (`tcpdump -i any -d` is `ldh [0]` first), so it is built: header 20 bytes, protocol first, `arp` allowed. DLT_NULL: the family word is in the capturing host's byte order (the FILE's, `Options.null_byte_order`, default this host's, `pcap.Reader.byteOrder()` gives the file's), compared as libpcap does for a savefile: `ip` is AF 2, `ip6` is 24, 28 or 30 (NetBSD/OpenBSD, FreeBSD, macOS; `gencode.c`, `rfile != NULL`), not Linux's 10. **Rejected:** PPP (a live Linux PPP device is DLT_LINUX_SLL in libpcap, `pcap-linux.c`, already built; only foreign PPP savefiles are left: no consumer), every other link type, other operating systems' capture, rpcap, USB, Bluetooth, D-Bus and RDMA capture sources (separate subsystems; none is AF_PACKET). 802.11 (radiotap, `wlan` qualifiers, monitor mode) is Backlog until a consumer asks.
- **`ip6 protochain` (and `ip protochain`): not built; the true reason.** libpcap compiles it to a loop with a `ja` that jumps BACKWARDS (`tcpdump -d 'ip6 protochain 6'`: `(018) ja 4`). The Linux kernel refuses that program at attach time, so it can never be a live filter (`tools/protochain_probe.py`, Linux 7.0, run with a control program that attaches: `ip6 protochain 6`, `ip6 protochain 44` and `ip protochain 6` all errno 22). libpcap's own USERSPACE interpreter does run it (`bpf_filter.c`: `pc += (bpf_int32)pc->k`, \"we currently implement ip6 protochain with backward jumps\"), so `pcap_offline_filter` filters a savefile with it. It is not built here because `filter.run` is loop-free by design (it terminates in `prog.len` steps, which is what lets it be total on hostile programs) and `validate` follows the kernel; a bounded unroll would not be libpcap's meaning.
- **Host names, service names, `gateway`, `ip broadcast`/`multicast`:** these need the resolver, /etc/ethers or the interface netmask, i.e. system state a pure compiler must not read; the caller passes numbers (`UnsupportedExpression`).
- **A BPF optimiser:** the code is longer than libpcap's with the same verdicts on all 190 tcpdump oracle rows (known deviations: offline `ip and vlan` without an id, which libpcap refuses and this compiles; live `ip and vlan 5`, where libpcap's own program accepts nothing and ours accepts the frame it names); the kernel runs both within noise (`filter_run_lp` vs `filter_run` is 0.67×: libpcap's programs are shorter, 1.5× faster to run in the same interpreter). A real, measurable gain, not built.
- **pcapng Name Resolution, Interface Statistics, Decryption Secrets and custom blocks:** skipped by length, not interpreted.
- **IPv6 Neighbor Discovery, BSD `/dev/bpf`:** unchanged from the survey (no consumer; the AF_PACKET ceiling).

- **2026-11-04 (done from the last review):** `Ring.release` identifies the held block by a ticket and its own memory (a stale or forged `Block` is `WrongBlock`); the vlan status bits are tested at the `struct tpacket3_hdr` offsets; `rawsock-ring-seq` checks a model of the cursor and `held`. Still open: `rawsock-validate` checks no-panic only, agreement with the kernel is the replayed table.
- **802.11** (radiotap, `wlan` qualifiers, monitor mode) and **foreign PPP savefiles**: return when a consumer asks.

- **2026-11-04 (mutation, schema, 27 mutants over names/shorthand grammar, `Ring.init` limits and the new link/live-vlan/ticket code):** 21 killed by the existing tests, 6 survived (a protocol name, an EtherType name, three size-limit edges accepted, the `block_nr` upper edge) and were killed after two new tests (every table name against its number; the limits accepted at their exact edge). Earlier schema 2026-11-03 (32 mutants on `run`, `validate`, long jumps, grammar subset, pcapng, ring): 31 killed, 1 equivalent (mutant 13: the both-sides-long jump branch cannot arise from the grammar). Not mutated: the live socket paths.

- **2026-10-30 (no-panic sweep GS):** `pcap.writeRecord` does not know the file's snaplen, so a record longer than `max(snaplen, 262144)` is written but `pcap.Reader` then refuses it (`RecordTooLong`). Not a crash; the writer should take the header's `snaplen` (a signature change) or refuse such a record. Decide with the consumer (axp-core does not use `pcap`). Also: the filter compiler caps a filter at `max_insns` comparisons while parsing (`FilterTooComplex`), so `Syntax` errors after that point are reported as `FilterTooComplex`.
- **FIXED 2026-11-03 (verified on mips32 BE soft-float under qemu: 0 failures; s390x not re-run): the seed encoders wrote native-endian length words, now `nativeToLittle`. Was: the two seed-corpus tests fail on s390x** (BE sweep 2026-10-18, same on Zig 0.16 and 0.17; re-run 2026-10-19 `-Dtarget=s390x-linux -fqemu -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe`): `corpus: the hwaddr seeds drive both shapes…` expected 7, found 0; `corpus: the ARP seeds…` expected 4, found 0. Test-only: the seeds are `std.testing.Smith` streams written on a little-endian host, so their length/choice words read differently on BE and no seed reaches the accepting arms. The parsers themselves are not involved. Fix: pin the counts per endianness, or encode the seeds through the Smith writer at comptime.

  a separate `pcapfile` module would need a root `build.zig` entry, and the codec is ~150 lines

- **Survey ranking** *(survey 2026-09-30)* — what a libpcap user hits first: (1) **pcap savefile read/write** (`.pcap`, later pcapng) — tcpdump interchange, and the natural test-fixture format; pure codec, small-medium; a separate `pcapfile` module may fit better than growing this one (no sibling exists: `ls modules | rg pcap` empty); (2) **a tcpdump-expression → classic-BPF compiler** (`tcp port 80 and host x`) — otherwise every filter is hand-assembled; medium-large, but pure Zig; (3) **per-frame kernel timestamp** (`SO_TIMESTAMPNS`/`PACKET_TIMESTAMP` cmsg, same path as `PACKET_AUXDATA` already parsed in `recv`); small; (4) `TPACKET_V3` ring and `PACKET_FANOUT` (already listed above); medium. All fit §2 (Linux-only stays an accepted ceiling).

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

- **Class A** — wire/interop format — other implementations must byte-agree with it.
- **Oracle EXTERNAL** — every wire or interop format the module speaks has bytes or verdicts from a foreign implementation or the kernel (below); the self-written residue is named.

**What the tests actually contain.** the `golden: real capture` tests in src/root.zig freeze a real ARP exchange and a real Ethernet/IPv4/ICMP frame captured with tcpdump off a veth pair in an unprivileged netns -- loopback cannot do ARP at all, which is why the pre-existing hand-computed fixture had never met a real L2 segment; since 2026-10-06 `arp.buildRequest` is anchored by the Linux kernel ANSWERING it (`unshare -rn zig build interop-rawsock -- --capture`: this module's `open`/`sendRaw`/`recv` on a veth pair, the kernel owning the target; request and the kernel's reply frozen in `src/testdata/kernel_arp.zig`, replayed by the "kernel ARP" test). The socket wrappers meet the kernel as a foreign peer only when that program runs (by hand); in the lane they stay self (loopback inject + capture of their own frames), which is the residue: those tests prove the wrappers move bytes, not that a foreign peer agrees. Anchored from outside since 2026-11-03: the filter compiler (100 expressions' frame verdicts from `tcpdump -r`, `run` over libpcap's own `-dd` programs; `tools/gen_filter_oracle.py`), classic pcap (two `tcpdump -w` files byte for byte) and pcapng (Wireshark `editcap` output decoded, this writer's output read by `tcpdump`/`capinfos`; `tools/gen_pcapng_fixtures.py`), the kernel's own filter verdict equal to `run` (netns lane), and the interface lookups against `ip` (`interop-rawsock`, by hand). Hand-computed only: `parseHwaddr`/`formatHwaddr` text forms and the `EthHeader` field edge cases (the header itself is also read off real captured frames).

**How it got there.** The anchoring work landed. DONE a326e4a: real ARP + IPv4 frames off a veth pair (loopback cannot do ARP)
